Density-based Sampling is a hierarchical sampling technique for neural radiance fields (NeRF) that optimizes computational cost by restricting network evaluations to geometrically relevant regions [S1].

The claim states that Density-based Sampling is a hierarchical sampling technique for NeRF that optimizes computational cost by restricting evaluations to geometrically relevant regions. The evidence in Source [S1] explicitly describes a method (attributed to Hu et al.) that evaluates the coarse NeRF MLP only at 'valid points' (positive densities) and the fine network at 'pivotal points' (densities exceeding a threshold). This description matches the 'hierarchical' aspect (coarse vs. fine networks) and the 'restricting network evaluations to geometrically relevant regions' aspect (positive densities/pivotal points). The evidence supports the core factual assertions of the claim.
supported
